title: How to Season a Cast-Iron Skillet

seo.title: How to Season a Cast-Iron Skillet
seo.meta_description: Season cast iron with an extremely thin film of oil and enough heat to polymerize it. Avoid excess oil that leaves the pan sticky.
seo.search_intent: Build or restore seasoning on a cast-iron skillet with a thin oil film and heat while avoiding a gummy finish.

excerpt: Seasoning is not a thick layer of grease. It is a nearly invisible film of oil transformed by heat into a bonded coating on the iron.
content_html:
Seasoning cast iron means polymerizing a very thin film of oil on the metal. The most common mistake is leaving too much oil, which creates sticky patches instead of a hard, even surface.

Clean and dry the pan completely

If you are restoring rust or residue, clean that first. Dry immediately, then warm the pan briefly over low heat to drive off moisture.

Apply less oil than you think

Use a cooking oil suitable for the process and recommended by the cookware maker. Coat the pan, then buff it with a clean cloth until it looks almost dry.

Heat it according to the manufacturer’s method

Many makers recommend baking the pan upside down at high heat for about an hour, then allowing controlled cooling. Ventilate the kitchen because some smoke is possible.

Repeat only when you need to build the base

A factory-preseasoned skillet may not need many immediate rounds. Cooking with fat and drying the pan well after use improves the surface over time.

If it is sticky, do not add more oil

Stickiness usually means the film was too thick or did not receive enough heat. Remove excess and repeat with a much thinner coat.

faq.question: Which oil should I use?
faq.answer: Use a cooking oil suitable for seasoning and follow the skillet manufacturer’s recommendation.

faq.question: Why is my pan sticky after seasoning?
faq.answer: Usually because too much oil was left on the surface or the layer did not fully polymerize.

faq.question: Do I need to season after every use?
faq.answer: No. Dry the pan thoroughly and add only a very light film of oil when needed.
